title: perf(canary): adaptive KV-aware hysteresis and rollout guards to reduce false positives
author: Priya Malhotra
description:
Motivation: Our performance canary has been producing noisy alerts during warm-up and when KV cache hit rates change between variants. This PR introduces adaptive thresholds and a small hysteresis window that is KV-cache aware to reduce false positives while preserving fast detection of real regressions.

What this changes: Implements KV-aware baseline selection (separate baselines for cold/warm cache profiles), adaptive percentile thresholds based on rolling distribution, and a configurable hysteresis window to avoid flip-flop during transient noise. Adds integration perf tests and dashboards + runbook updates.

Checklist:
- [x] Add KV-aware baseline computation and storage
- [x] Add adaptive percentile-based thresholding (p95/p99 with dynamic multipliers)
- [x] Add hysteresis state machine and rollout guard enforcement
- [x] Add unit + integration perf tests
- [x] Update canary dashboard and alerting playbook
- [x] End-to-end smoke in staging

Related: ENG-5432 (perf canary improvements), ENG-5490 (canary flapping during model warm-up), SUP-1284 (support case: false positive canary alert for 2.x runtime)
commits: 5 commits: 1) compute: add kv cache profile tagging and baseline buckets; 2) detector: adaptive percentile thresholds and multiplier tuning; 3) hysteresis: introduce state machine and cooldown timer; 4) tests: add perf canary integration tests and fixtures; 5) docs: dashboard and runbook updates
diff_snippets: detector.py: introduced adaptive_threshold() which computes dynamic threshold based on rolling p95/p99 and a multiplier tuned per latency distribution; hysteresis_state.py: small state machine (STABLE -> WARNING -> DEGRADED) with cooldown timers; kv_profile.py: tag requests with kv_cache_state and maintain two baselines (cold/warm)
review_comments:
Ethan Park: Can we make the hysteresis window configurable per-deployment? - Response (Priya): yes, added a deploy-level override and sane defaults in thresholds.yml.

Lina Gomez: Tests look good but add a case where KV hit-rate changes mid-run to ensure we don't trigger on expected shift - Response: added test_kv_profiles.py to simulate a warmup flip and ensure baseline switch is gradual.

Marco Rossi: How will this affect existing alerts? - Response: dashboard + runbook updated; we will roll out guarded on canary namespace only for 48h and monitor.

Lina Gomez: approved. Ethan Park: approved.
ci_summary: CI: unit tests (pass), lint (pass), perf-smoke (pass in staging), end-to-end (pass, flake-free). A single unrelated flaky test was retried and passed.
release_notes: Improved performance canary detection: adaptive thresholds and KV-cache-aware hysteresis reduce false positive alerts during model warm-up and cache state changes; adds rollout guards to avoid canary flip-flop. Backwards compatible; configurable per-deployment.
files_reviewed_highlights:
- redwood/observability/canary/detector.py: uses rolling-window histograms and dynamic multipliers for p95/p99 thresholds.
- redwood/observability/canary/kv_profile.py: class KVProfileStore persists cold/warm baselines.
- redwood/observability/canary/hysteresis_state.py: state machine with cooldowns and percent-sustained criteria.
testing_notes: Added o11y/perf-canary integration test that runs synthetic request traces with configurable KV hit rates; new tests validate no-alert for warmup transitions and rapid detection for true latency regressions. Tests run in ~90s on CI perf runner.
deploy_plan: Phase 1: Rollout to canary namespace only for 48h with monitoring on p95/p99 and KV hit-rate metrics. Phase 2: If stable, flip a runtime flag to enable in staging for 24h. Phase 3: Gradual rollout to production with 10% traffic increments and automatic rollback on canary->degraded state. Manual playbook in redwood/docs/runbooks/perf-canary.md.
post_merge_actions: Monitor the perf canary dashboard for 72h, notify #sre if any canary enters DEGRADED state. Remove staging-only flag after 7d if no regressions. Update customer-facing changelog if any external-facing alerts change.
notes_for_releaser: This is a safe backend-only change. Use squash merge, tag canary deploy at release candidate, follow deploy_plan. No migration required. Thresholds.yml contains defaults that may be tuned per-customer.
auditor_comments: Security review: no new secrets or network changes. Observability reviewer: good coverage, ensure runbook links added to alert messages.
